question:
Xuri Company has signed delivery contracts for 5 products $(i=1, \cdots, 5)$ for the next year from January to June. It is known that the order quantity (in units), unit selling price (in yuan), unit cost (in yuan), and production hours required for each product are $D_i, S_i, C_i, a_i$, respectively. The normal production hours and maximum allowable overtime hours for each month from January to June are shown in Table 1-19.
Table 1-19
\begin{tabular}{c|r|r|r|r|r|r}
\hline Month & \multicolumn{1}{|c|}{1} & \multicolumn{1}{|c|}{2} & \multicolumn{1}{|c}{3} & \multicolumn{1}{|c}{4} & \multicolumn{1}{c}{5} & \multicolumn{1}{c}{6} \\
\hline Normal Production Hours $/ \mathrm{h}$ & 12000 & 11000 & 13000 & 13500 & 13500 & 14000 \\
\hline Maximum Allowable Overtime Hours $/ \mathrm{h}$ & 3000 & 2500 & 3300 & 3500 & 3500 & 3800 \\
\hline
\end{tabular}

However, the cost of each product produced during overtime hours increases by $C_i^{\prime}$ yuan. Due to production preparation and delivery requirements, product 1 is scheduled to start production in March, product 3 needs to be delivered by the end of April, and product 4 can be produced starting from February and must be fully delivered by the end of May. If products 3 and 4 are delayed in delivery, a penalty of $p_3$ yuan and $p_4$ yuan per month of delay will be imposed, respectively. All products must be delivered by the end of June. Please design a production plan for the company that guarantees completion of the contracts and maximizes profit, and establish a mathematical model.

"""
PRODUCTION PLANNING WITH OVERTIME, DELIVERY WINDOWS AND DELAY PENALTIES
=======================================================================

SETS / INDICES
  I = {1,...,5}      products
  M = {1,...,6}      months (January .. June)

DECISION VARIABLES
  x[i,m]   units of product i produced in month m during NORMAL hours
           domain: NonNegativeIntegers, bounds (0, D_i)
  y[i,m]   units of product i produced in month m during OVERTIME hours
           domain: NonNegativeIntegers, bounds (0, D_i)
  late3    months of delay for product 3 (delivered after end of April)
           domain: NonNegativeIntegers, bounds (0, 2)   [April->May->June]
  late4    months of delay for product 4 (delivered after end of May)
           domain: NonNegativeIntegers, bounds (0, 1)   [May->June]

OBJECTIVE (maximize profit)
  revenue  = sum_i S_i * D_i
  minus normal production cost  sum_{i,m} C_i * x[i,m]
  minus overtime production cost sum_{i,m} (C_i + C'_i) * y[i,m]
  minus delay penalties p_3*late3 + p_4*late4

CONSTRAINTS
  (1) Demand satisfaction:  sum_m (x[i,m]+y[i,m]) = D_i            for all i
  (2) Normal hours:         sum_i a_i * x[i,m] <= H_norm[m]        for all m
  (3) Overtime hours:       sum_i a_i * y[i,m] <= H_ot[m]          for all m
  (4) Product 1 starts in March: x[1,m]=y[1,m]=0 for m in {1,2}
  (5) Product 3 delivered by end of April (+delay):
        sum_{m<=4}(x[3,m]+y[3,m]) >= D_3 - (D_3/2)*late3
      (linearised: production in first 4 months covers all but the delayed part)
  (6) Product 4 starts from February: x[4,1]=y[4,1]=0
  (7) Product 4 delivered by end of May (+delay):
        sum_{m<=5}(x[4,m]+y[4,m]) >= D_4 - (D_4/1)*late4
  (8) All products delivered by end of June (implied by (1) over M).
"""

import pyomo.environ as pyo

DATA = {
    # products 1..5
    "D": {1: 3000, 2: 2500, 3: 2000, 4: 2200, 5: 1800},   # order quantity (units)
    "S": {1: 120, 2: 110, 3: 130, 4: 125, 5: 100},        # unit selling price (yuan)
    "C": {1: 70, 2: 65, 3: 80, 4: 75, 5: 60},             # unit cost (yuan)
    "Cp": {1: 15, 2: 12, 3: 18, 4: 16, 5: 10},            # overtime cost increase (yuan)
    "a": {1: 3, 2: 2, 3: 4, 4: 3, 5: 2},                  # production hours per unit
    # months 1..6
    "H_norm": {1: 12000, 2: 11000, 3: 13000, 4: 13500, 5: 13500, 6: 14000},
    "H_ot":   {1: 3000,  2: 2500,  3: 3300,  4: 3500,  5: 3500,  6: 3800},
    # delay penalties per month of delay (yuan)
    "p3": 5000,
    "p4": 4000,
    # delivery windows
    "p1_start_month": 3,          # product 1 may start in March
    "p3_deadline_month": 4,       # product 3 due end of April
    "p4_start_month": 2,          # product 4 may start in February
    "p4_deadline_month": 5,       # product 4 due end of May
    "p3_max_delay": 2,            # April -> May -> June
    "p4_max_delay": 1,            # May -> June
    "p3_delay_unit": 1000,        # units of product 3 short per month of delay
    "p4_delay_unit": 1100,        # units of product 4 short per month of delay
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA

    products = list(d["D"].keys())
    months = list(d["H_norm"].keys())

    m = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    m.I = pyo.Set(initialize=products)
    m.M = pyo.Set(initialize=months)

    # ---- decision variables ----
    m.x = pyo.Var(m.I, m.M, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers,
                  bounds=lambda mm, i, t: (0, d["D"][i]))
    m.y = pyo.Var(m.I, m.M, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers,
                  bounds=lambda mm, i, t: (0, d["D"][i]))
    m.late3 = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers,
                      bounds=(0, d["p3_max_delay"]))
    m.late4 = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers,
                      bounds=(0, d["p4_max_delay"]))

    # ---- objective: maximize profit ----
    revenue = sum(d["S"][i] * d["D"][i] for i in products)
    normal_cost = sum(d["C"][i] * m.x[i, t] for i in products for t in months)
    overtime_cost = sum((d["C"][i] + d["Cp"][i]) * m.y[i, t]
                        for i in products for t in months)
    penalty = d["p3"] * m.late3 + d["p4"] * m.late4

    m.obj = pyo.Objective(
        expr=revenue - normal_cost - overtime_cost - penalty,
        sense=pyo.maximize,
    )

    # ---- (1) demand satisfaction ----
    def demand_rule(mm, i):
        return sum(mm.x[i, t] + mm.y[i, t] for t in mm.M) == d["D"][i]
    m.demand = pyo.Constraint(m.I, rule=demand_rule)

    # ---- (2) normal hours ----
    def normal_hours_rule(mm, t):
        return sum(d["a"][i] * mm.x[i, t] for i in mm.I) <= d["H_norm"][t]
    m.normal_hours = pyo.Constraint(m.M, rule=normal_hours_rule)

    # ---- (3) overtime hours ----
    def overtime_hours_rule(mm, t):
        return sum(d["a"][i] * mm.y[i, t] for i in mm.I) <= d["H_ot"][t]
    m.overtime_hours = pyo.Constraint(m.M, rule=overtime_hours_rule)

    # ---- (4) product 1 starts in March ----
    def p1_start_rule(mm, t):
        if t < d["p1_start_month"]:
            return mm.x[1, t] + mm.y[1, t] == 0
        return pyo.Constraint.Skip
    m.p1_start = pyo.Constraint(m.M, rule=p1_start_rule)

    # ---- (5) product 3 delivered by end of April (+delay) ----
    def p3_deadline_rule(mm):
        early = sum(mm.x[3, t] + mm.y[3, t]
                    for t in mm.M if t <= d["p3_deadline_month"])
        return early >= d["D"][3] - d["p3_delay_unit"] * mm.late3
    m.p3_deadline = pyo.Constraint(rule=p3_deadline_rule)

    # ---- (6) product 4 starts from February ----
    def p4_start_rule(mm, t):
        if t < d["p4_start_month"]:
            return mm.x[4, t] + mm.y[4, t] == 0
        return pyo.Constraint.Skip
    m.p4_start = pyo.Constraint(m.M, rule=p4_start_rule)

    # ---- (7) product 4 delivered by end of May (+delay) ----
    def p4_deadline_rule(mm):
        early = sum(mm.x[4, t] + mm.y[4, t]
                    for t in mm.M if t <= d["p4_deadline_month"])
        return early >= d["D"][4] - d["p4_delay_unit"] * mm.late4
    m.p4_deadline = pyo.Constraint(rule=p4_deadline_rule)

    return m

import pyomo.environ as pyo

DATA = {
    # Products 1..5: order quantity D_i (units)
    "D": {1: 5000, 2: 4000, 3: 3000, 4: 6000, 5: 4500},   # order quantity (units)
    # Unit selling price S_i (yuan)
    "S": {1: 120, 2: 150, 3: 200, 4: 100, 5: 130},        # unit selling price (yuan)
    # Unit cost C_i (yuan)
    "C": {1: 80, 2: 95, 3: 130, 4: 65, 5: 85},            # unit cost (yuan)
    # Overtime cost increase C'_i (yuan)
    "Cp": {1: 20, 2: 25, 3: 35, 4: 15, 5: 22},            # overtime unit cost increase (yuan)
    # Production hours per unit a_i (h)
    "a": {1: 2.0, 2: 2.5, 3: 3.0, 4: 1.5, 5: 2.2},        # production hours per unit (h)
    # Normal production hours per month (h)
    "Hnorm": {1: 12000, 2: 11000, 3: 13000, 4: 13500, 5: 13500, 6: 14000},
    # Maximum allowable overtime hours per month (h)
    "Omax": {1: 3000, 2: 2500, 3: 3300, 4: 3500, 5: 3500, 6: 3800},
    # Delay penalties per month (yuan)
    "p3": 4000,   # penalty for product 3 per month of delay (yuan)
    "p4": 3000,   # penalty for product 4 per month of delay (yuan)
    # Scheduling windows
    "p1_start": 3,     # product 1 scheduled to start in March
    "p4_start": 2,     # product 4 can be produced starting from February
    "p3_deadline": 4,  # product 3 delivered by end of April
    "p4_deadline": 5,  # product 4 fully delivered by end of May
    "T_last": 6,       # all delivered by end of June
    "bigM": 1e9,       # big-M for linearisation
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    I = list(d["D"].keys())
    T = list(d["Hnorm"].keys())

    m = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    m.I = pyo.Set(initialize=I)
    m.T = pyo.Set(initialize=T)

    # Normal-time production units x[i,t]
    m.x = pyo.Var(m.I, m.T, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    # Overtime production units y[i,t]
    m.y = pyo.Var(m.I, m.T, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # Delay months for products 3 and 4 (integer)
    m.z3 = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers, bounds=(0, 2))
    m.z4 = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers, bounds=(0, 1))

    # ---- Objective: maximize profit ----
    def obj_rule(m):
        revenue = sum(d["S"][i] * (m.x[i, t] + m.y[i, t])
                      for i in m.I for t in m.T)
        cost = sum(d["C"][i] * (m.x[i, t] + m.y[i, t])
                   for i in m.I for t in m.T)
        overtime = sum(d["Cp"][i] * m.y[i, t]
                       for i in m.I for t in m.T)
        penalty = d["p3"] * m.z3 + d["p4"] * m.z4
        return revenue - cost - overtime - penalty

    m.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.maximize)

    # ---- Normal hours capacity each month ----
    def norm_hours_rule(m, t):
        return sum(d["a"][i] * m.x[i, t] for i in m.I) <= d["Hnorm"][t]

    m.norm_hours = pyo.Constraint(m.T, rule=norm_hours_rule)

    # ---- Overtime hours capacity each month ----
    def ot_hours_rule(m, t):
        return sum(d["a"][i] * m.y[i, t] for i in m.I) <= d["Omax"][t]

    m.ot_hours = pyo.Constraint(m.T, rule=ot_hours_rule)

    # ---- Demand satisfaction ----
    def demand_rule(m, i):
        return sum(m.x[i, t] + m.y[i, t] for t in m.T) == d["D"][i]

    m.demand = pyo.Constraint(m.I, rule=demand_rule)

    # ---- Product 1 starts in March: no production Jan/Feb ----
    def p1_window_rule(m, t):
        if t < d["p1_start"]:
            return m.x[1, t] + m.y[1, t] == 0
        return pyo.Constraint.Skip

    m.p1_window = pyo.Constraint(m.T, rule=p1_window_rule)

    # ---- Product 4 starts from February: no production in January ----
    def p4_window_rule(m, t):
        if t < d["p4_start"]:
            return m.x[4, t] + m.y[4, t] == 0
        return pyo.Constraint.Skip

    m.p4_window = pyo.Constraint(m.T, rule=p4_window_rule)

    # ---- Completion indicators ----
    m.w3 = pyo.Var(m.T, within=pyo.Binary)
    m.w4 = pyo.Var(m.T, within=pyo.Binary)

    def cum3_rule(m, t):
        return sum(m.x[3, k] + m.y[3, k] for k in m.T if k <= t)

    def cum4_rule(m, t):
        return sum(m.x[4, k] + m.y[4, k] for k in m.T if k <= t)

    # w3[t] = 1 iff cumulative production by t >= D3
    def w3_def_a(m, t):
        return cum3_rule(m, t) >= d["D"][3] - d["bigM"] * (1 - m.w3[t])

    def w3_def_b(m, t):
        return cum3_rule(m, t) <= d["D"][3] + d["bigM"] * (1 - m.w3[t])

    m.w3_def_a = pyo.Constraint(m.T, rule=w3_def_a)
    m.w3_def_b = pyo.Constraint(m.T, rule=w3_def_b)

    def w4_def_a(m, t):
        return cum4_rule(m, t) >= d["D"][4] - d["bigM"] * (1 - m.w4[t])

    def w4_def_b(m, t):
        return cum4_rule(m, t) <= d["D"][4] + d["bigM"] * (1 - m.w4[t])

    m.w4_def_a = pyo.Constraint(m.T, rule=w4_def_a)
    m.w4_def_b = pyo.Constraint(m.T, rule=w4_def_b)

    # Monotonicity of completion indicators
    def w3_monotone_rule(m, t):
        if t == min(m.T):
            return pyo.Constraint.Skip
        prev = max(k for k in m.T if k < t)
        return m.w3[t] >= m.w3[prev]

    m.w3_monotone = pyo.Constraint(m.T, rule=w3_monotone_rule)

    def w4_monotone_rule(m, t):
        if t == min(m.T):
            return pyo.Constraint.Skip
        prev = max(k for k in m.T if k < t)
        return m.w4[t] >= m.w4[prev]

    m.w4_monotone = pyo.Constraint(m.T, rule=w4_monotone_rule)

    # Number of months from completion month to June inclusive
    def w3_count_rule(m):
        return sum(m.w3[t] for t in m.T) == d["T_last"] - (d["p3_deadline"] + m.z3) + 1

    m.w3_count = pyo.Constraint(rule=w3_count_rule)

    def w4_count_rule(m):
        return sum(m.w4[t] for t in m.T) == d["T_last"] - (d["p4_deadline"] + m.z4) + 1

    m.w4_count = pyo.Constraint(rule=w4_count_rule)

    # Deadline enforcement using w
    def p3_deadline_rule(m, t):
        return cum3_rule(m, t) >= d["D"][3] * m.w3[t]

    m.p3_deadline = pyo.Constraint(m.T, rule=p3_deadline_rule)

    def p4_deadline_rule(m, t):
        return cum4_rule(m, t) >= d["D"][4] * m.w4[t]

    m.p4_deadline = pyo.Constraint(m.T, rule=p4_deadline_rule)

    return m

    # Products 1..5
    "products": [1, 2, 3, 4, 5],
    # Months 1..6 (Jan..Jun)
    "months": [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6],

    # Order quantity D_i (units)
    "D": {1: 1000, 2: 1200, 3: 900, 4: 1100, 5: 800},

    # Unit selling price S_i (yuan/unit)
    "S": {1: 200, 2: 220, 3: 180, 4: 210, 5: 190},

    # Unit cost C_i (yuan/unit) during normal hours
    "C": {1: 120, 2: 130, 3: 110, 4: 125, 5: 115},

    # Overtime cost increment C'_i (yuan/unit)
    "Cp": {1: 30, 2: 35, 3: 25, 4: 32, 5: 28},

    # Production hours required per unit a_i (h/unit)
    "a": {1: 10, 2: 12, 3: 9, 4: 11, 5: 8},

    # Normal production hours per month
    "Hnorm": {1: 12000, 2: 11000, 3: 13000, 4: 13500, 5: 13500, 6: 14000},

    # Maximum allowable overtime hours per month
    "Hover": {1: 3000, 2: 2500, 3: 3300, 4: 3500, 5: 3500, 6: 3800},

    # Penalty per month of delay (yuan/unit/month)
    "p": {3: 15, 4: 18},

    # Earliest production start month per product (product 1 -> March, product 4 -> Feb)
    "start": {1: 3, 2: 1, 3: 1, 4: 2, 5: 1},

    # Latest delivery month per product (product 3 -> April, product 4 -> May, else June)
    "due": {1: 6, 2: 6, 3: 4, 4: 5, 5: 6},

    # Big-M for delay linearisation (max possible units of a product)
    "M": 100000,
}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# MODEL
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA

    m = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    m.I = pyo.Set(initialize=d["products"], ordered=True)
    m.T = pyo.Set(initialize=d["months"], ordered=True)

    # x[i,t] : units of product i produced in month t during normal hours
    m.x = pyo.Var(m.I, m.T, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # y[i,t] : units of product i produced in month t during overtime hours
    m.y = pyo.Var(m.I, m.T, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # z[i,t] : units of product i delivered in month t (delivery schedule)
    m.z = pyo.Var(m.I, m.T, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # delay[i] : number of months product i is delayed beyond its due month
    m.delay = pyo.Var(m.I, domain=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers, bounds=(0, len(d["months"])))

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Constraints
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    # (1) Production only allowed from the product's start month onward.
    def rule_prod_window(m, i, t):
        if t < d["start"][i]:
            return m.x[i, t] + m.y[i, t] == 0
        return pyo.Constraint.Skip

    m.prod_window = pyo.Constraint(m.I, m.T, rule=rule_prod_window)

    # (2) Total production of each product equals its order quantity.
    def rule_demand(m, i):
        return sum(m.x[i, t] + m.y[i, t] for t in m.T) == d["D"][i]

    m.demand = pyo.Constraint(m.I, rule=rule_demand)

    # (3) Total deliveries of each product equal its order quantity.
    def rule_deliver_all(m, i):
        return sum(m.z[i, t] for t in m.T) == d["D"][i]

    m.deliver_all = pyo.Constraint(m.I, rule=rule_deliver_all)

    # (4) Cumulative deliveries cannot exceed cumulative production (no early delivery).
    def rule_cum_delivery(m, i, t):
        return (
            sum(m.z[i, tau] for tau in m.T if tau <= t)
            <= sum(m.x[i, tau] + m.y[i, tau] for tau in m.T if tau <= t)
        )

    m.cum_delivery = pyo.Constraint(m.I, m.T, rule=rule_cum_delivery)

    # (5) Deliveries only allowed up to the product's due month plus delay.
    #     z[i,t] <= M * indicator(t <= due[i] + delay[i])
    #     Linearised: t - due[i] - delay[i] <= M * (1 - w[i,t]) with z <= M*w
    #     Simpler: enforce z[i,t] = 0 for t > due[i] + delay[i] via big-M.
    def rule_delivery_window(m, i, t):
        # t <= due[i] + delay[i]  <=>  t - due[i] - delay[i] <= 0
        # If violated, force z[i,t] = 0.
        return m.z[i, t] <= d["M"] * pyo.max if False else m.z[i, t] <= d["M"]

    # Replace with proper linear big-M formulation using binary w[i,t]
    m.w = pyo.Var(m.I, m.T, domain=pyo.Binary)

    def rule_delivery_window2(m, i, t):
        # w[i,t] = 1 means delivery in month t is permitted
        # t - due[i] - delay[i] <= M * (1 - w[i,t])
        return t - d["due"][i] - m.delay[i] <= d["M"] * (1 - m.w[i, t])

    m.delivery_window = pyo.Constraint(m.I, m.T, rule=rule_delivery_window2)

    def rule_delivery_link(m, i, t):
        return m.z[i, t] <= d["M"] * m.w[i, t]

    m.delivery_link = pyo.Constraint(m.I, m.T, rule=rule_delivery_link)

    # (6) Normal production hours capacity per month.
    def rule_normal_hours(m, t):
        return sum(d["a"][i] * m.x[i, t] for i in m.I) <= d["Hnorm"][t]

    m.normal_hours = pyo.Constraint(m.T, rule=rule_normal_hours)

    # (7) Overtime production hours capacity per month.
    def rule_overtime_hours(m, t):
        return sum(d["a"][i] * m.y[i, t] for i in m.I) <= d["Hover"][t]

    m.overtime_hours = pyo.Constraint(m.T, rule=rule_overtime_hours)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Objective: maximise profit
    #   revenue  = sum_i S_i * D_i
    #   cost     = sum_{i,t} C_i * x[i,t] + (C_i + C'_i) * y[i,t]
    #   penalty  = sum_i p_i * delay[i] * D_i
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    revenue = sum(d["S"][i] * d["D"][i] for i in m.I)

    prod_cost = sum(
        d["C"][i] * m.x[i, t] + (d["C"][i] + d["Cp"][i]) * m.y[i, t]
        for i in m.I for t in m.T
    )

    penalty = sum(
        d["p"][i] * m.delay[i] * d["D"][i]
        for i in m.I if i in d["p"]
    )

    m.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=revenue - prod_cost - penalty, sense=pyo.maximize)

    return m

    "months": [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6],
    "demand":      {1: 500,  2: 800,  3: 600,  4: 700,  5: 400},
    "sell_price":  {1: 220,  2: 180,  3: 250,  4: 300,  5: 160},
    "unit_cost":   {1: 120,  2: 100,  3: 140,  4: 170,  5: 90},
    "ot_premium":  {1: 20,   2: 15,   3: 25,   4: 30,   5: 12},
    "hours":       {1: 2,    2: 1.5,  3: 2.5,  4: 3,    5: 1},
    "normal_hours": {1: 12000, 2: 11000, 3: 13000, 4: 13500, 5: 13500, 6: 14000},
    "max_ot_hours": {1: 3000,  2: 2500,  3: 3300,  4: 3500,  5: 3500,  6: 3800},
    "delay_penalty": {3: 4000, 4: 5000},
    "start_month": {1: 3, 2: 1, 3: 1, 4: 2, 5: 1},
    "deadline": {1: 6, 2: 6, 3: 4, 4: 5, 5: 6},
    "max_delay": {3: 2, 4: 1},
    "bigM": 100000,
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    P = d["products"]
    T = d["months"]

    m = pyo.ConcreteModel()
    m.I = pyo.Set(initialize=P)
    m.T = pyo.Set(initialize=T)

    # x[i,t]: total units of product i produced in month t
    m.x = pyo.Var(m.I, m.T, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)
    # o[i,t]: units of product i produced during overtime in month t
    m.o = pyo.Var(m.I, m.T, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)
    # y[t]: overtime hours used in month t
    m.y = pyo.Var(m.T, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals,
                  bounds=lambda m, t: (0, d["max_ot_hours"][t]))
    # z3, z4: delay months for products 3 and 4
    m.z3 = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers,
                   bounds=(0, d["max_delay"][3]))
    m.z4 = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers,
                   bounds=(0, d["max_delay"][4]))

    # overtime units cannot exceed total units
    def rule_ot_le_total(m, i, t):
        return m.o[i, t] <= m.x[i, t]
    m.c_ot_le_total = pyo.Constraint(m.I, m.T, rule=rule_ot_le_total)

    # total overtime hours in month <= overtime available
    def rule_ot_hours(m, t):
        return sum(d["hours"][i] * m.o[i, t] for i in m.I) <= m.y[t]
    m.c_ot_hours = pyo.Constraint(m.T, rule=rule_ot_hours)

    # monthly normal hours limit on normal portion
    def rule_normal_hours(m, t):
        return sum(d["hours"][i] * (m.x[i, t] - m.o[i, t]) for i in m.I) \
            <= d["normal_hours"][t]
    m.c_normal_hours = pyo.Constraint(m.T, rule=rule_normal_hours)

    # production cannot start before the start month
    def rule_start(m, i, t):
        if t < d["start_month"][i]:
            return m.x[i, t] == 0
        return pyo.Constraint.Skip
    m.c_start = pyo.Constraint(m.I, m.T, rule=rule_start)

    # For products 3 and 4 the effective delivery month is deadline + z.
    # Linearise: cumulative production up to deadline >= demand - bigM * z
    # (delay relaxes the base requirement), and cumulative production up to
    # deadline + max_delay >= demand (must be met within the horizon).
    def rule_deadline_base(m, i):
        if i in (3, 4):
            z = m.z3 if i == 3 else m.z4
            base = sum(m.x[i, t] for t in m.T if t <= d["deadline"][i])
            return base >= d["demand"][i] - d["bigM"] * z
        return pyo.Constraint.Skip
    m.c_deadline_base = pyo.Constraint(m.I, rule=rule_deadline_base)

    def rule_deadline_full(m, i):
        if i in (3, 4):
            full = sum(m.x[i, t] for t in m.T
                       if t <= d["deadline"][i] + d["max_delay"][i])
            return full >= d["demand"][i]
        return pyo.Constraint.Skip
    m.c_deadline_full = pyo.Constraint(m.I, rule=rule_deadline_full)

    # all production complete by end of June
    def rule_june(m, i):
        return sum(m.x[i, t] for t in m.T) >= d["demand"][i]
    m.c_june = pyo.Constraint(m.I, rule=rule_june)

    # objective: revenue - normal cost - overtime premium - delay penalties
    def obj_rule(m):
        revenue = sum(d["sell_price"][i] * m.x[i, t] for i in m.I for t in m.T)
        cost = sum(d["unit_cost"][i] * m.x[i, t] for i in m.I for t in m.T)
        premium = sum(d["ot_premium"][i] * m.o[i, t] for i in m.I for t in m.T)
        penalty = d["delay_penalty"][3] * m.z3 + d["delay_penalty"][4] * m.z4
        return revenue - cost - premium - penalty
    m.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.maximize)

    return m

    # Product allowed latest production month
    "latest_month": {1: 6, 2: 6, 3: 4, 4: 5, 5: 6},
    # Allowed month pair list precomputed window check
    "on_time_product_3_deadline": 4,
    "on_time_product_4_deadline": 5,
    "delay4_months": 1,  # two months late margin: penalties scaled by months
    "delay3_months": 1,
}


def build_model(data=None):

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.products = pyo.Set(initialize=d["products"])
    model.months = pyo.Set(initialize=d["months"])

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Decision variables
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def x_bounds(m, i, t):
        if d["earliest_month"][i] <= t <= d["latest_month"][i]:
            return (0, None)
        return (0, 0)

    def y_bounds(m, i, t):
        if d["earliest_month"][i] <= t <= d["latest_month"][i]:
            return (0, None)
        return (0, 0)

    model.x = pyo.Var(model.products, model.months,
                      within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers, bounds=x_bounds)
    model.y = pyo.Var(model.products, model.months,
                      within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers, bounds=y_bounds)

    # Delay shortfall (units not delivered on time)
    model.g3 = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeReals, bounds=(0, d["D"][3]))
    model.g4 = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeReals, bounds=(0, d["D"][4]))

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Demand fulfilment
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def demand_rule(m, i):
        return sum(m.x[i, t] + m.y[i, t] for t in m.months) == d["D"][i]

    model.demand = pyo.Constraint(model.products, rule=demand_rule)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Monthly normal-hour capacity
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def normal_hours_rule(m, t):
        return sum(d["a"][i] * m.x[i, t] for i in m.products) <= d["normal_hours"][t]

    model.normal_cap = pyo.Constraint(model.months, rule=normal_hours_rule)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Monthly overtime-hour capacity
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def overtime_hours_rule(m, t):
        return sum(d["a"][i] * m.y[i, t] for i in m.products) <= d["overtime_hours"][t]

    model.ot_cap = pyo.Constraint(model.months, rule=overtime_hours_rule)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Product 3 on-time (by end April)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    dl3 = d["on_time_product_3_deadline"]

    def ontime3_rule(m):
        return sum(m.x[3, t] + m.y[3, t]
                   for t in m.months if t <= dl3) >= d["D"][3] - m.g3

    model.ontime3 = pyo.Constraint(rule=ontime3_rule)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Product 4 on-time (by end May)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    dl4 = d["on_time_product_4_deadline"]

    def ontime4_rule(m):
        return sum(m.x[4, t] + m.y[4, t]
                   for t in m.months if t <= dl4) >= d["D"][4] - m.g4

    model.ontime4 = pyo.Constraint(rule=ontime4_rule)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Objective: revenue - cost - overtime premium - delay penalty
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def objective_rule(m):
        normal_profit = sum(
            (d["S"][i] - d["C"][i]) * m.x[i, t]
            for i in m.products for t in m.months
        )
        overtime_profit = sum(
            (d["S"][i] - d["C"][i] - d["Cp"][i]) * m.y[i, t]
            for i in m.products for t in m.months
        )
        penalty = d["p3"] * m.g3 + d["p4"] * m.g4
        return normal_profit + overtime_profit - penalty

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=objective_rule, sense=pyo.maximize)

    return model

import pyomo.environ as pyo

DATA = {
    # products i = 1..5 : order quantity D, selling price S, unit cost C, hours a
    "products": [1, 2, 3, 4, 5],
    "months": [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6],
    "D": {1: 3000, 2: 2500, 3: 2000, 4: 1800, 5: 2200},   # order quantity (units)
    "S": {1: 120, 2: 150, 3: 200, 4: 180, 5: 160},        # unit selling price
    "C": {1: 60, 2: 80, 3: 100, 4: 90, 5: 85},            # unit normal cost
    "Cp": {1: 15, 2: 20, 3: 25, 4: 22, 5: 18},            # overtime cost increase
    "a": {1: 3, 2: 2, 3: 4, 4: 3, 5: 2},                  # hours per unit
    # normal production hours per month
    "normal_hours": {1: 12000, 2: 11000, 3: 13000, 4: 13500, 5: 13500, 6: 14000},
    # max allowable overtime hours per month
    "max_overtime": {1: 3000, 2: 2500, 3: 3300, 4: 3500, 5: 3500, 6: 3800},
    # penalty per month of delay
    "p": {3: 5000, 4: 4000},
    # earliest month a product may be produced
    "earliest": {1: 3, 2: 1, 3: 1, 4: 2, 5: 1},
    # deadline month (must be fully delivered by end of this month)
    "deadline": {1: 6, 2: 6, 3: 4, 4: 5, 5: 6},
    # big-M for delay binary linking (large enough vs. any feasible delay)
    "M": 6,
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    products = d["products"]
    months = d["months"]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # Sets
    model.I = pyo.Set(initialize=products)          # products
    model.M = pyo.Set(initialize=months)            # months
    # allowed product-month production pairs (respect earliest start & deadline)
    pairs = [(i, m) for i in products for m in months
             if d["earliest"][i] <= m <= d["deadline"][i]]
    model.PM = pyo.Set(initialize=pairs, dimen=2)

    # Variables
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.PM, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)   # normal-hour units
    model.y = pyo.Var(model.PM, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)   # overtime units

    # delay months for products 3 and 4 (integer)
    model.z = pyo.Var([3, 4], domain=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers, bounds=(0, None))
    # binary: whether product i is delivered late
    model.late = pyo.Var([3, 4], domain=pyo.Binary)

    # Objective: maximise profit = revenue - normal cost - overtime cost - penalties
    def obj_rule(m):
        revenue = sum(d["S"][i] * (m.x[i, mm] + m.y[i, mm])
                      for (i, mm) in m.PM)
        cost_n = sum(d["C"][i] * m.x[i, mm] for (i, mm) in m.PM)
        cost_o = sum((d["C"][i] + d["Cp"][i]) * m.y[i, mm] for (i, mm) in m.PM)
        penalty = sum(d["p"][i] * m.z[i] for i in [3, 4])
        return revenue - cost_n - cost_o - penalty

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.maximize)

    # Demand satisfaction: total production of each product = order quantity
    def demand_rule(m, i):
        return sum(m.x[i, mm] + m.y[i, mm] for mm in m.M if (i, mm) in m.PM) == d["D"][i]
    model.demand = pyo.Constraint(model.I, rule=demand_rule)

    # Normal hours capacity per month
    def normal_rule(m, mm):
        return sum(d["a"][i] * m.x[i, mm] for i in m.I if (i, mm) in m.PM) \
            <= d["normal_hours"][mm]
    model.normal_cap = pyo.Constraint(model.M, rule=normal_rule)

    # Overtime hours capacity per month
    def overtime_rule(m, mm):
        return sum(d["a"][i] * m.y[i, mm] for i in m.I if (i, mm) in m.PM) \
            <= d["max_overtime"][mm]
    model.overtime_cap = pyo.Constraint(model.M, rule=overtime_rule)

    # Delay linking: z_i <= M * late_i  (z positive forces late = 1)
    def delay_link_rule(m, i):
        return m.z[i] <= d["M"] * m.late[i]
    model.delay_link = pyo.Constraint([3, 4], rule=delay_link_rule)

    return model
